group_assessment.weighting: A mouse-genetics group (Jackson Laboratory, from the affiliations) with long-standing HDL QTL work. Primary for mouse HDL QTL mapping; not primary for WWOX or for any WWOX disease. Observation (resequencing, qPCR, QTL overlap) weighed above the interpretive sentences about WWOX, which rest on one predicted missense change.

entries.proposition: The human input is a published three-cohort GWA meta-analysis (8,816 individuals); the paper is a mouse bioinformatics and resequencing re-analysis, not a new human or WWOX-null measurement.
entries.snippet: The dataset included the results from the association analysis between the genotypes of approximately 2.5 million SNPs (genotyped and inferred) and the phenotype (HDL levels) for 8,816 individuals.

entries.proposition: WWOX enters the paper as a suggestive GWA hit, P = 2.25e-5, far above the genome-wide line of 5e-8 that the paper itself names for the significant loci.
entries.snippet: at 117 Mb for Wwox (P = 2.25 × 10−5 in the GWA)
entries.anchor: Results, Mouse evidence for novel genes

entries.proposition: The paper defines its significant loci at P below 5e-8 and its suggestive SNPs at P below 1e-3.
entries.snippet: investigating the seven significant loci (104 SNPs with P < 5 × 10−8 as well as suggestive SNPs, defined as P < 10−3.
entries.anchor: Results, Mapping of GWA study genes

entries.proposition: Liver expression of Wwox did not differ between the QTL parental strains B6 and CAST by real-time PCR.
entries.snippet: For Wwox, we performed real-time PCR between B6 and CAST on chow in males and females but did not find any difference in expression (P > 0.05) (Table 1).

entries.proposition: The only Wwox evidence offered is one predicted-functional missense change, V186M.
entries.snippet: However, by resequencing, we identified a nonsynonymous coding polymorphism predicted to change function (V186M) in an exon present in four out of the five transcripts reported in Ensembl

entries.proposition: The conclusion that Wwox is a QTL gene for the B6xCAST cross rests on the stated possibility that V186M 'may affect' function.
entries.snippet: because V186M may affect the function or structure of WWOX, we think that Wwox is a QTL gene for the B6xCAST cross.

entries.proposition: V186M does not segregate in the second cross, B6xCASA.
entries.snippet: The polymorphism segregated between B6 and CAST but not between B6 and CASA.

entries.proposition: Table 1 scores V186M as functional by SIFT only and as not conserved; the PolyPhen column is not scored for it.
entries.snippet: Wwox B6xCAST C F −1.16 (0.342) V186M No Yes (SIFT) No

entries.proposition: The candidate-gene interval for the B6xCAST cross still holds 184 genes after haplotype filtering.
entries.snippet: haplotype analysis reduced the number of candidate genes to 184 for the B6xCAST cross (including Cdh13 and Wwox) and 154 for the B6xCASA cross (including Galnt2)

entries.proposition: For the positive-control gene Abca1 the paper adds an expression difference and a promoter-reporter assay; nothing comparable is offered for Wwox.
entries.snippet: By luciferase assay, we extended this observation by showing that a cis-acting element in the promoter region controls the Abca1 mRNA expression (Fig. 2D)

entries.proposition: The Discussion states that the Wwox knockout mouse is hypercholesterolemic and infers raised HDL; this is the sign opposite to the one a companion human paper attributes to the same mouse.
entries.snippet: For instance, the Wwox knockout mouse has previously been shown to exhibit hypercholesterolemia (39); HDL was not measured, but hypercholesterolemia in a chow-fed mouse would indicate increased HDL because 80% to 90% of cholesterol in a chow-fed mouse is HDL.

entries.proposition: Reference 39, cited for that statement, is the 2007 Wwox knockout tumor-suppressor paper.
entries.snippet: Targeted deletion of Wwox reveals a tumor suppressor function.

entries.proposition: In the cited paper the serum lipid change of the null mouse is reported only as 'data not shown'; no cholesterol value is printed there. (Rendered page 4 of the cited paper, read as an image because its PDF text layer has no ToUnicode map.)
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Page 4 of Aqeilan et al. 2007 (PNAS 104:3952), Discussion, first paragraph, right column: 'Blood chemistry analysis of homozygous mice showed marked alterations in serum levels of proteins, carbohydrates, and lipids (data not shown).'
entries.anchor: Aqeilan 2007 page 4, Discussion paragraph 1, rendered at 100 dpi

entries.proposition: The Discussion says the mouse confirms cis-regulation of WWOX, although the Results report no expression difference for Wwox by real-time PCR.
entries.snippet: Molecular evidence in human populations that suggests cis-regulation of WWOX (42) and FADS1 (7) is confirmed by our results in the mouse.

entries.proposition: The authors name species differences in HDL metabolism as a limit of the strategy, including the absence of CETP in the mouse.
entries.snippet: A limitation of our strategy is the existence of important species differences in HDL metabolism, such as the absence of the CETP gene in the mouse.

entries.proposition: Supplementary Table S4: the WWOX GWA bin is a 27.6 kb block whose lead SNP is rs2667590 at 77,088,538 (build 36), P 2.25e-5 - a different intron-8 position from the rs2548861 and Saez regions.

entries.snippet: e One probe set for Wwox (1431960_at) in our 12-strain microarray survey indicated a significant difference in expression between B6 and CAST, but this difference was due to the presence of a polymorphism at the probe binding site.
